market_holds: Spot about $1.46-1.49 (baseline 18:08 UTC $1.46, a 52-week low, -43% from the high, -8.75% over 5d, -11% over 20d). No usable option chain, so I have no implied move. I used Yahoo daily bars for the gap at the next US open after the last three prints: Q3'25 (2025-11-24 amc) -6.1% at the open, then a +8.9% close; Q1'26 (2026-05-11) -4.1%; Q2'26 (2026-08-24) -1.7% at the open, then a +1.7% close. The 5d fall roughly tracks China internet and the tape: KWEB -4.4%, FXI -4.7%, and SPY -2.2% with a -3.6% day on 11-20. 2391.HK fell -8.6% over 5 sessions. Consensus for Q3'26 is EPS $0.03 and revenue of about $95.5-95.8M, which is +16% YoY on Q3'25's $82.5M and +2.8% QoQ (Benzinga and Yahoo, per a search snippet, undated). That is the Q2 growth rate carried forward. There is no numeric guide; on the Q2 call management said gross margin 'expected to stabilize'. The balance sheet holds $976M of cash and investments with no debt (2026-06-30) against about 610M shares, so market cap is about $890M, below net cash. No interim dividend has been confirmed for 2026, while one was paid in Sep 2025; the March 2026 dividend was $0.0605. A 10% buyback mandate exists, but only $1.6M was bought in H1. The HK line trades on the release before the US open, so the scored open will carry the Hong Kong session's verdict.
view: Tuya is a cash-rich, thinly covered IoT PaaS company priced below net cash. Consensus asks it to repeat Q2's +16% growth. The inputs I could see neither clearly beat that bar nor clearly miss it. In favour: the YoY comp is easy (Q3'25 grew +1.1%), Q2 beat its revenue estimate by about 6% ($92.9M vs $87.8M), and Espressif, the leading Wi-Fi MCU supplier, pre-announced Q3 revenue +32-35% with margins 'at a good level' (2026-10-16). Against: Espressif said its own smart-home demand was 'broadly stable', with growth coming from non-smart-home areas. Tuya's own Q2 call flagged North American price sensitivity and a Middle East pause. Semiconductor input costs have pushed Tuya's gross margin down about 2pp YoY in both Q1 and Q2, and nothing shows that pressure eased in Q3. Revenue growth in line with consensus and another dip in gross margin is the base case, and it looks priced. Possible upside surprises are a capital-return step (a resumed dividend, or real use of the buyback below cash) or a revenue beat like Q2's. The main downside risk is a margin step-down from memory and flash costs. US opens after recent prints have leaned negative, but they reflect the HK session and the macro tape as much as the release. I cannot see a side the price does not hold.

recommendation.reason: The bar is revenue of about $95.5M (+16% YoY), a straight extrapolation of Q2. The peer and supply-chain evidence I found (Espressif strong, but smart-home 'broadly stable'; Tuya's own NA and Middle East caution; ongoing chip-cost pressure on margin) is mixed and does not make either side of that line more likely than the price assumes. The below-cash valuation limits downside but is not a catalyst inside an overnight window. With no implied move and no dated datapoint since August that consensus has not absorbed, there is no mechanism to bet on.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A capital-return announcement in the release, such as a resumed or enlarged dividend or a sizeable buyback executed below cash, would point up. A gross margin well below 46% with no stabilisation language would point down.

self_critique: Upside case: the stock trades below net cash after an 8.75% slide at a 52-week low. Q2 beat revenue by about 6%, the YoY comp is trivial, Espressif's IoT channel was strong, and any capital-return news or another beat could squeeze a thin float. Downside case: two quarters of margin erosion amid a semiconductor cost cycle, NA weakness, the missing interim dividend, and recent negative opens after prints. Each case carries similar weight, so 50 stands.
approach_notes: P4/P6 helped by separating the tape-driven 5d fall from company news and by treating the below-cash valuation as a bar rather than a reason. The thin baseline (no options, no history) made P2 step 1 rely on my own price pull. The peer-first route (Espressif) paid off most, but it was not decisive.
